config.title: table layout

intro.title: table layout
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a clean, structured data table to display product information using CSS table layout properties. You will learn how to use display: table, table-row, and table-cell to create table-like structures without HTML table elements. The main technologies involved are CSS display properties and basic styling techniques. This approach gives you more flexibility than traditional HTML tables while maintaining proper alignment and structure. By the end, you'll understand how to create responsive, semantic table layouts using pure CSS.
intro.usecase: Table layout is essential for displaying structured data across countless real-world applications. You'll find it in e-commerce product comparison tables, financial dashboards showing stock portfolios, and admin panels displaying user management data. As a developer, you'll use table layout techniques to create data-rich interfaces like pricing comparison charts, inventory management systems, and analytics reports where information needs clear organization. Mastering table layout ensures you can present complex datasets in a readable, professional format that users can quickly scan and understand.

objectives: Construct a basic HTML table structure with rows and columns
Apply CSS properties to control table border appearance and spacing
Configure table header cells with distinct styling from data cells
Implement alternating row colors using CSS pseudo-class selectors
Manipulate table width and cell alignment to control layout proportions
Initialize responsive table behavior for different screen sizes
Integrate caption and summary elements for table accessibility

steps.title: Create a basic HTML table structure in the CSS file
steps.instruction: Add a basic HTML table structure with table, thead, tbody, tr, th, and td elements in the CSS file
steps.hint: You can add HTML comments in CSS files to describe the structure that will be styled. Use a comment block to outline the table elements.
steps.seedCode: /* Add your HTML table structure comment here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file containing an HTML table structure comment that will serve as the foundation for styling
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a comment with table, thead, tbody, tr, th, and td elements
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You have some of the required elements. Make sure your comment includes table, thead, tbody, tr, th, and td elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS file doesn't contain the required HTML table structure comment. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Apply basic table styling with border and width
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that targets the table element and sets a solid border and a width of 100%.
steps.hint: Use the table selector followed by curly braces, then add border and width properties inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: The table will have a visible border and occupy the full width of its container.
successCriteria: The table selector has a border property set to a solid style and a width property set to 100%.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both border and width properties to the table selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're targeting the table element correctly and have included both border and width properties.

steps.title: Style table headers with background color and padding
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to style the table header cells (th) with a background color and padding.
steps.hint: Use the th selector to target table header cells. Set background-color to a color like #f2f2f2 and padding to a value like 8px.
steps.expectedOutcome: The table headers will have a light gray background and consistent padding around their content.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for th elements is added with both background-color and padding properties set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a rule for th, but make sure to include both background-color and padding properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for th elements is missing or incomplete. Add a rule with background-color and padding.

steps.title: Add padding and border to table cells
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for table data cells (td) that sets padding to 8px and adds a 1px solid black border.
steps.hint: Use the td selector to target all table data cells. Inside the rule, set the padding and border properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: Table data cells will have consistent padding and a visible border around each cell.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for td elements exists with padding: 8px; and border: 1px solid black; properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included both the padding and border properties for the td selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for table data cells is missing or incomplete. Please add a rule for td with padding and border properties.

steps.title: Implement table border-collapse property
steps.instruction: Add the border-collapse property to the table rule and set it to 'collapse' to merge cell borders.
steps.hint: The border-collapse property controls whether table borders are separated or collapsed into a single border.
steps.expectedOutcome: The table's cell borders will be merged into single borders instead of separate borders.
successCriteria: The table rule includes border-collapse: collapse; property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the border-collapse property, but check if you set it to 'collapse' to properly merge borders.
steps.feedbackWrong: The border-collapse property is missing or incorrect. Add border-collapse: collapse; to the table rule.

steps.title: Add zebra striping to table rows
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to style even-numbered table rows with a light background color using the nth-child selector.
steps.hint: Use the selector 'tr:nth-child(even)' and set a background-color property.
steps.expectedOutcome: Even-numbered table rows will have a light background color, creating a zebra-striped effect.
successCriteria: A CSS rule using 'tr:nth-child(even)' with a background-color property is added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using 'tr:nth-child(even)' and setting a background-color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The zebra striping rule is missing or incorrect. Try using 'tr:nth-child(even)' with a background-color property.

steps.title: Center align table content
steps.instruction: Add the text-align property to center the text inside all table headers and table data cells.
steps.hint: Use the text-align property with the value 'center' on both th and td selectors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The text inside all table headers and cells will be horizontally centered.
successCriteria: CSS rules are added to center align text in both th and td elements using the text-align property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to apply text-align: center to both th and td selectors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The text in the table headers and cells should be centered. Try adding text-align: center to both th and td.

steps.title: Add hover effect to table rows
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that changes the background color of table rows when the user hovers over them using the :hover pseudo-class.
steps.hint: Use the selector 'tr:hover' and set a background-color property to a color of your choice (e.g., lightgray).
steps.expectedOutcome: The table rows will change background color when hovered over, providing visual feedback.
successCriteria: A CSS rule with the selector 'tr:hover' is added and includes a background-color property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've used the ':hover' pseudo-class and set a background-color property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hover effect is not implemented correctly. Check that you've used 'tr:hover' and defined a background-color.

steps.title: Set table width to 100% and add margin
steps.instruction: Add a width property to the table selector to make it full width, and add a margin property for spacing.
steps.hint: Set width: 100%; and margin: 20px auto; inside the table selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The table will stretch to the full width of its container and have spacing around it.
successCriteria: The table selector includes width: 100%; and margin: 20px auto;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both width: 100%; and margin: 20px auto; to the table selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table selector should include width: 100%; and margin: 20px auto; to achieve full width and spacing.

steps.title: Add border-radius to table and cells for rounded corners
steps.instruction: Add a border-radius property to the table selector to give the entire table rounded corners.
steps.hint: Use the border-radius property with a value like 8px or 10px to create rounded corners on the table.
steps.expectedOutcome: The table will have rounded corners, giving it a more modern and polished appearance.
successCriteria: The table selector includes a border-radius property with a value like 8px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the border-radius property to the table selector with a value like 8px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table doesn't have rounded corners yet. Add a border-radius property to the table selector.
